title: The Cross of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The cross of Christ is the place where Jesus suffered and died for sinners, displaying the seriousness of sin, the justice of God, the love of God, and the saving power of the Gospel.
summary: The cross of Christ is the place where Jesus suffered and died for sinners, displaying the seriousness of sin, the justice of God, the love of God, and the saving power of the Gospel.
christFocus: Jesus Christ willingly endured the cross to redeem His people. The cross reveals His obedience, sacrifice, shame-bearing love, and victory over sin, condemnation, and the powers of darkness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The cross was an instrument of shame and death, yet God made it the center of salvation. Jesus humbled Himself and became obedient to death, even death on a cross.

At the cross, Christ suffered for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring people to God. The cross is not merely a tragedy; it is the saving work of God.

The cross also displays victory. By His death, Christ cancels the record of debt against His people and triumphs over the powers that accuse and enslave.

The message of the cross appears foolish to the world, but to those being saved it is the power of God. The church must never move beyond the cross as though it were elementary or embarrassing.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the cross, Christianity becomes moral advice, religious activity, or vague spirituality. The cross shows that sin is deadly serious and that God’s love is costly beyond measure.

This doctrine gives hope to the ashamed. Christ bore shame openly so guilty people could be forgiven and reconciled to God. The cross is where condemnation is answered and mercy is given.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Boast in the cross of Christ. Bring your guilt, shame, pride, and fear to the crucified Savior. Do not preach or live a crossless faith. Let the cross shape your worship, repentance, forgiveness, endurance, and love for others.
